_: An equation, and — if it carries an `expression` — a calculator generated from this record. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the four extra rules a computable formula must satisfy.
name: C-rate from an applied current
_expression: Optional. Present = the workbench offers a calculator. Parsed by js/lib/expr.js (never eval). Every symbol must appear in variables[], every variable must declare units[], and result.units[] is required — all four are ERRORS if missing.

variables.name: Nominal capacity
variables.note: Theoretical capacity, manufacturer rating, or the capacity this electrode actually delivered? The three give different currents for '1C' and the basis must be stated.

_variables: units[].f is the factor converting that unit to siUnit. mg→kg is 1e-6. Check these by hand: the health check verifies the expression parses, not that your arithmetic is right, and mAh/g is 3600 rather than 3.6.

validContext.note: 1C nominally means the full nominal capacity in one hour. Whether Q_nominal is theoretical, rated or measured changes the meaning entirely.

_validContext: REQUIRED. cellType, deviceConfig, performanceLevel, and a note saying what a reader would otherwise get wrong. The single-electrode and symmetric-device forms of the same quantity differ by a factor of four.
assumptions: Q_nominal is defined on the same basis as the current is applied — per gram of active material, or per cell.
The nominal capacity is appropriate to this material and window, not carried over from another chemistry.
limitations: A convenience, not a physical property. Two laboratories quoting 1C for the same material can be applying different currents.
For materials with no well-defined nominal capacity — most carbons in supercapacitor use — current density is the clearer quantity.
A C-rate defined against the wrong nominal capacity is a common route to an unintended overcurrent.
_limitations: Every equation has conditions it fails under. A record with none warns.
